hints.title: Head Deletion Boundary Obstacle
hints.text: Removing the leading node requires special head updates. How can a sentinel node standardize node removal across every position in the list?

hints.title: Sentinel Lookahead Deletion Invariant
hints.text: Use a dummy head pointing to head. Traverse with curr: if curr.next.val equals val, bypass curr.next; otherwise, advance curr.

hints.title: Single-Pass Splicing Procedure
hints.text: Create dummy with next pointing to head. Set curr to dummy. While curr.next is not null: if curr.next.val == val, set curr.next to curr.next.next; else, advance curr to curr.next. Return dummy.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass removing matching value nodes in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Special-casing head deletions often leads to null pointer exceptions or misses consecutive matching nodes at the front.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using a sentinel dummy node eliminates all head branch conditions without extra auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean sentinel dummy node usage and ensuring curr is not advanced when a deletion occurs.
